answer: Concretely, the economy can meter the marginal energy cost of each new identity against the network's median. Near-duplicate embeddings collapse the farm into one cluster. Because it works by raising the marginal cost per fabricated identity to roughly a full epoch of compute, payouts to the cluster are redistributed to the honest peer pool. An identity earns only when its cipher recurs, its pulse survives audit, and a opal from an unlinked peer confirms it.
